author: Ari Koslow
title: Nick Kurtz (illness) considered day-to-day
desc: Nick Kurtz is considered day-to-day after leaving Wednesday's game early with an illness.
impact: Athletics manager Mark Kotsay said Kurtz was throwing up in the dugout. "I don't think there's much in his stomach right now," he said.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Willson Contreras day-to-day with foot contusion
desc: Willson Contreras is day-to-day with a left foot contusion.
impact: Contreras left Wednesday's game early after fouling a pitch off his left foot. It appears he avoided anything too significant.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tim Herrin (elbow) has X-rays return negative
desc: Tim Herrin underwent X-rays that came back negative for any fractures.
impact: Herrin took a comebacker off his pitching elbow during Wednesday's game against the Twins. He is day-to-day going into Thursday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Dillon Dingler (hand) has X-rays return negative
desc: Dillon Dingler had X-rays return negative for any fractures.
impact: Dingler will continue to undergo further imaging. He is day-to-day going into Thursday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Anthony Seigler (trap) exits early Wednesday
desc: Anthony Seigler was removed from Wednesday's game against the White Sox with a right trap contusion.
impact: Seigler suffered the injury on a collision at home plate. He will be further evaluated into Thursday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Pablo Reyes signs minor league deal with Angels
desc: The Angels signed INF Pablo Reyes to a minor league contract.
impact: Reyes was most recently with the Padres. He will add infield depth in the Angels organization.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Riley Unroe signs minor league deal with White Sox
desc: The White Sox signed INF Riley Unroe to a minor league contract.
impact: Unroe will add infield depth in the White Sox organization.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Colin Rea picks up win Wednesday
desc: Colin Rea allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out two across 5.1 innings in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: While Rea allowed seven hits, his most since his June 9 start at Coors Field, he was still able to limit the Orioles to three runs and pick up his second straight win. He owns a 4.75 ERA and 1.45 WHIP with 70 strikeouts across 94.2 innings this season. Rea will not make another start until after the All-Star break.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Seiya Suzuki hits homer Wednesday
desc: Seiya Suzuki went 1-for-4 with a home run, one run scored and three RBI in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: Suzuki entered Wednesday's contest in the midst of a four-game hitless streak but snapped it in a big way, launching a 401-foot, three-run homer off Grant Wolfram in the seventh inning. While he has struggled to begin July, Suzuki has had a strong season overall, slashing .260/.342/.449 with 14 home runs.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Michael Conforto goes yard Wednesday
desc: Michael Conforto went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: Conforto launched a 368-foot homer off Dean Kremer in the fifth inning, marking his eighth home run of the season. Although he has had a limited role this season while primarily starting against right-handed pitching, he has been excellent to begin July, going 7-for-18 with three homers, five runs scored and five RBI.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong belts two homers Wednesday
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong went 2-for-4 with two home runs, a walk, three runs scored and two RBI in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: Crow-Armstrong launched two homers off Dean Kremer on Wednesday, hitting a 377-foot shot in the third inning and a 419-foot blast in the fifth. He has been one of the top outfielders in baseball this season, as he's tied for third among outfielders with 21 home runs while leading the position with 23 stolen bases. He owns a .296 AVG and .928 OPS through 92 games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Nico Hoerner swipes bag Wednesday
desc: Nico Hoerner went 0-for-3 with a walk and a stolen base in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: While Hoerner did not record a hit on Wednesday, he still provided fantasy managers with some production by drawing a walk in the second inning and stealing second base. He has struggled to begin July, slashing .190/.250/.238 across 21 at-bats, but he has at least recorded a stolen base in back-to-back games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Carson Kelly connects for homer Wednesday
desc: Carson Kelly went 1-for-3 with a home run, a walk, two runs scored and an RBI in Wednesday's 9-7 win over the Baltimore Orioles.
impact: Kelly launched a 404-foot homer off Dean Kremer in the fifth inning, connecting for his fifth home run of the season. He has started in three games in July and is 3-for-9 with three walks and three runs scored during that stretch. On the season, he owns a .283 AVG and .779 OPS across 66 games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Kyle Stowers launches homer Wednesday
desc: Kyle Stowers went 1-for-3 with a solo home run in Wednesday's 2-0 win over the Mariners.
impact: Stowers launched a 416-foot homer off George Kirby in the second inning, marking his 12th home run of the season. He has been one of Miami's hottest hitters over his last 15 games, slashing .322/.379/.712 with five homers.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Tyler Phillips picks up win Wednesday
desc: Tyler Phillips allowed no runs on four hits and two walks while striking out three across five innings in Wednesday's 2-0 win over the Mariners.
impact: After allowing five runs in his July 3 start against the Athletics, Phillips bounced back in a big way on Wednesday, tossing five scoreless innings while needing just 71 pitches. Following the outing, he owns a 4.58 ERA and 1.35 WHIP with 25 strikeouts across 39.1 innings as a starter. He is not scheduled to make another start until after the All-Star break.
